answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind collateral at an ingress jetty and route verification flows across a network wharf. Peer nodes perform topological cut verifications and multi-agent auditing; any inconsistent partition proofs trigger stake slashing, driving the attacker's capital to its nadir. Because isolating cut boundaries forces the creation of bipartite paths, an adversary faces superlinear attacker cost scaling with network size.
